# Books

A Quarto book gets one index for the whole book, not one per chapter — and
every index the book declares, in every format, each printed where its own
marker stands. See [Named indexes](named-indexes.qmd) for how a book declares
more than one. Write the placement marker in the chapter that should hold it:

```markdown
::: {.qi-index-here}
:::
```

Everything below, down to the last section, is about the **HTML book**: it is
the one Quarto renders a chapter at a time. A PDF or EPUB book goes through a
single Pandoc process, so none of it applies — see the last section.

**Put that chapter last.** Quarto renders an HTML book's chapters in order,
and each chapter is a separate render that cannot see the others, so the index
is built from the chapters that ran before the one holding the marker. Put the
marker anywhere else and the chapters after it are represented by whatever the
*previous* render recorded: on a first render they are missing, and after an
edit their entries can name terms the chapter no longer marks and link to
anchors its page no longer has. The extension names those chapters every time
it builds the index, so this is loud rather than silent — but the fix is to
move the marker, not to render twice.

In the HTML book, each entry's locators link to the chapters that mark the
term, in book order — across files, and across subdirectories, from wherever
the index chapter sits. A cross-reference links to its target entry whenever
some chapter in the book contributes it, so `see=` works across chapters
exactly as it does inside one document.

A book that declares several indexes prints each index some chapter files a
mark in, each at the first marker naming it — in whichever chapter that marker
stands — and any index no marker names after them, in declared order, at the
end of the book's last chapter. Every judgement the extension makes across
chapters is made inside one index, so a `see=` written in one index that names
a term only another index marks is reported as naming nothing indexed, and the
report says which index it was judged in.

The last chapter is where an index no marker names goes whatever the book's
markers say, provided some chapter of the book places an index at all. That
chapter is the end of the book's own chapter list, which every chapter of
every render reads the same way, so which chapter carries the section does not
change from one render to the next. Where the last chapter carries a marker of
its own, the section follows the ones its markers place; where it carries
none, the section goes at the end of that chapter. A book with no marker
anywhere places no index and grows no section in its last chapter either.

Adding or moving a placement marker changes where the indexes that marker
names are printed, and nothing else: a chapter that gains a marker for an
index prints that index from the very next render, and the index no marker
names stays where it was.

Two things worth knowing:

- **Render the whole book when you publish.** Rendering a single chapter
  updates that chapter's marks only; the index is rebuilt from what the last
  full render recorded for the others. `quarto render` with no file argument
  is what makes the index current.
- **A book with marks but no marker chapter gets no index**, and says so once
  per render, naming the marker to add. The extension will not choose a
  chapter for you.

Each chapter records its marks in `.quarto/quarto-index/` inside your project —
Quarto's own scratch directory, alongside the caches Quarto keeps there, and
never copied into `_book/`. There is nothing to configure. A project created
with `quarto create project` already ignores `/.quarto/` in git; a book whose
`_quarto.yml` you wrote by hand may not, and that one line is worth adding.

If a chapter's record cannot be written or read back — a read-only project
tree, a stale file where the directory belongs, a record left by an older
version of this extension — the book still renders, and the extension names
the chapter whose terms are missing from the index. Rendering that chapter
again is the fix. A record that names an index you have since removed from
`indexes:` costs nothing: its marks are filed in the first index the book
still declares, and the report names the chapter and the name.

Either report repeats: the book draws it once for every chapter that builds an
index section, which is what the unusable record costs it. A chapter that
builds none reports too where the records it read show no chapter of the book
placing an index — a book with no placement marker anywhere, and equally a
chapter rendered while the record of the chapter carrying the marker cannot
itself be read.

## The merged books: PDF and EPUB

A PDF book and an EPUB book need none of the above. Quarto renders each as one
merged document, so the extension sees every chapter's marks at once: there is
no per-chapter record, nothing to keep current, and the marker may go in any
chapter. A PDF book's `makeindex` has always had every chapter's marks at once,
and the printed index gathers page numbers from all of them. An EPUB book
prints every index its `indexes:` metadata declares, each under its own title,
and a page range opened in one chapter and closed in another pairs — see the
[EPUB](epub.qmd) page.
